propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui sanctum Camillum, ad animarum in extremo agone luctantium
subsidium, singulari caritatis praerogativa decorasti: ejus, quaesumus,
meritis, spiritum nobis tuae dilectionis infunde; ut in hora exitus nostri
hostem vincere, et ad caelestem mereamur coronam pervenire. Per Dominum
nostrum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

translations.text: O God, Who didst adorn blessed Camillus with a special gift of charity for the help of souls struggling in their last agony, pour upon us, we beseech Thee, by his merits, the spirit of Thy love, that in the hour of our death we may be worthy to overcome the enemy and attain unto the heavenly crown. Through our Lord.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Hostia immaculata, qua illud Domini nostri Jesu Christi immensae caritatis
opus renovamus, sit, Deus Pater omnipotens, sancto Camillo intercedente,
contra omnes corporis et animae infirmitates salutare remedium, et in
extremo agone solacium et tutela. Per eundem Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum,
Filium tuum: Qui tecum.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text: May the unblemished sacrifice, by which we renew that work of the boundless love of our Lord Jesus Christ, be, O God, almighty Father, through Saint Camillus's intercession, a saving remedy against all illnesses of body and soul, and comfort and protection in the final struggle. Through the same Jesus Christ our Lord, your Son: who with you.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Per haec caelestia alimenta, quae, sancti Camilli Confessoris tui solemnia
celebrantes, pia devotione suscepimus: da, quaesumus, Domine; ut, in hora
mortis nostrae sacramentis refecti et culpis omnibus expiati, in sinum
misericordiae tuae laeti suscipi mereamur: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre
in unitate.

translations.text: Through this heavenly nourishment which we have received with pious devotion, in celebrating the solemnity of blessed Camillus, Thy confessor, grant, we beseech Thee, O Lord, that in the hour of our death, refreshed by Thy sacraments, and all our sins forgiven, we may deserve to be taken up, rejoicing, into the bosom of Thy mercy. Who livest.
